items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: So anyone, Osie and I were very good friends.

ctx.x: Yeah, he says that. When you associate with somebody like that, you... I guess you are helping them in a way. Yeah, I don't remember things that he said. But he and I worked together, and by me being the pianist, perhaps he would talk to me about some chord or some voicing. You know, when you're young like that, unless you've got some kind of ego to say, "Well, I helped do this..." I have a lot of musicians that I know give me a lot of credit for having done this and that, and a lot of times I don't even…

I think a person learns from every musician that he works with. Just because he was playing a couple of years longer, or ten years or whatever, it doesn't mean that you can't learn something from another musician. See, I teach now, and I've taught my students "You think that you're studying from me. I'm studying from you at the same time!"
